_what: The control schemes: the shape of a game on a screen — what hands do — one per game, declared as SCHEME in the game's own config/controls.js. `seed` is the controls file this scheme starts from, copied in at creation and never replaced; `title` and `what` are the words New game and the Controls panel show. This file doubles as the validation list, the way game-templates/index.json does for templates. The other file in here, achievements.js, is the achievements library's seed and has nothing to choose.
_offer: What is offered, in order. An entry naming a family stands for the family: New game offers the family, and the Controls panel offers its manners underneath. A family is an interface grouping and never a word in the file — SCHEME is always one concrete scheme, because a file claiming to be arcade would not say which shape a phone actually gets.
_default: What a game is seeded with when nobody picks: the null controller, which draws nothing. ⚠️ It must name the same file as the input library's own seed in studio-lib/index.json, which is what an install with no choice at all writes; test/schemes.test.js holds the two together.

arcade.title: Arcade
arcade.what: Held like a games machine: a stick, or buttons, or both, drawn on the screen for a phone. Which of those is up to you, and you can change it later.

none.title: Just the game's own buttons
none.what: The buttons on the page are the controls. Nothing is drawn on top, and they work the same for a mouse, a finger and the keyboard. Right for a quiz, a story, or anything you press rather than steer.

stick-buttons.title: A stick and buttons
stick-buttons.what: A stick under one thumb to move, round buttons under the other. What most games want.

buttons.title: Buttons only
buttons.what: Arrows under one thumb, buttons under the other, nothing analog. A button can latch, so turning, thrusting and firing can all happen at once.

dual-stick.title: Two sticks
dual-stick.what: One stick to move and one to aim, so you can shoot one way while running another.

one-button.title: One button
one-button.what: The whole screen is the button: a tap or a click anywhere, nothing drawn. For flapping, jumping and games about timing.

swipe-tap.title: Swipes and taps
swipe-tap.what: Flick the screen to move, tap it to act. For sliding puzzles, snake and matching games.
